### pull in michigan data from second data transfer -- transferred on 12/15
read_excel_allsheets <- function(filename) { 
  sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(filename) 
  x <- lapply(sheets, function(X) readxl::read_excel(filename, sheet = X)) 
  names(x) <- sheets 
  x 
}

                     pattern = "*CSG_JJ_01-01-2015 through 12-31-2020_121321.xlsx",

```{r include=FALSE}
### join all files together using data table diagram as visual guide using left join, starting with child_details -- our base demo file
 
###### de-dup child_details using PERSON_ID
child_details %<>%
  distinct(PERSON_ID,.keep_all = TRUE) ### file already unique by PERSON_ID; no records dropped 

###### de-dup placements using all columns
placements <- new_placements %<>%
  distinct(.,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(PLACEMENT_BEGIN_DATE = ymd(PLACEMENT_BEGIN_DATE))### file already unique; no pure duplicates and no records dropped 

### inner join placements to child_details -- dropping records from child_details with no matching placement data
child_details_placements <- inner_join(child_details, placements, by = "PERSON_ID")

### IGNORE incidents FOR NOW -- NEED TO CLEAN + PIVOT WIDE BEFORE MERGING; MAY NEED TO ANALYZE SEPARATELY -- NOT JOINED TO MAIN ANALYTIC FILE AS I NEED TO EXPLORE HOW AND IF WE CAN JOIN INCIDENTS TO SPECIFIC PLACEMENTS + CASES

###### de-dup incidents using all columns
incidents %<>%
  distinct(.,.keep_all = TRUE) ### file already unique; no pure duplicates and no records dropped

### join incidents to child_details to obtain race/ethnicity and gender -- may eventually need to join to placement data in order to calculate incidents per placements by facility and facility type, though
child_details_incidents <- inner_join(child_details, incidents, by = c("PERSON_ID"))


# For now, I've coded the following legal statuses as dual ward, based on Mike's feedback: 
# 52 - MCI Ward/44 and Act 150/46 -- mdhhs (abuse/neglect whose rights have been terminated and delinquent public ward under act 150 w/ mdhhs)
# 90 - Temp Court Ward 42 and Delinquent Court Ward 40 -- uncertain (a/n temp court and delinquent court ward; use other field for court, mdhhs, can change over time)
# 91 -  Perm Court Ward 41 and Delinquent Court Ward 40 -- uncertain ()
# 92 - Temp Court Ward 42 and Act 150/46 -- mdhhs
# 93 - Perm Court Ward 41 and Act 150/46 -- mdhhs
# 94 - MCI Ward/44 and Delinquent Court Ward/40 -- uncertain
# 80 - In Home 42 and Delinquent Court Ward 40 -- uncertain
# 82 - In Home 42 and Act 150/46 -- mdhhs
# 
# And the following as state wards based on Soleil's feedback (according to Soleil, "Both the 40 and the 50 are MDHHS supervised youth, not county court supervised. The 50 is the legal status fort given when an intake is done in MiSACWIS until another status is added based on a court order or the youth may be a pre sentence investigation"):
# 40 - Court Ward Delinquent -- mdhhs
# 44 - State Ward ' MCI - Act 220/296
# 46 - State Ward - Delinquent - Act 150 -- mdhhs
# 50 - Non-Ward With a Delinquent Petition Filed -- either intake, juvenile competency, or pretrial investigations AND likely mdhhs supervised

### create three lists for dual, state, and county wards with the corresponding legal_status codes 
dual_ward_status_list <- c("52 - MCI Ward/44 and Act 150/46","90 - Temp Court Ward 42 and Delinquent Court Ward 40","91 -  Perm Court Ward 41 and Delinquent Court Ward 40","92 - Temp Court Ward 42 and Act 150/46","93 - Perm Court Ward 41 and Act 150/46","94 - MCI Ward/44 and Delinquent Court Ward/40","80 - In Home 42 and Delinquent Court Ward 40","82 - In Home 42 and Act 150/46")

state_ward_status_list <- c("40 - Court Ward Delinquent","44 - State Ward ' MCI - Act 220/296", "46 - State Ward - Delinquent - Act 150","50 - Non-Ward With a Delinquent Petition Filed")

county_ward_status_list <- c()

###### de-dup legal_status using all columns
###### for legal statuses with same start date (n = 120ish), I keep the legal status with the longer window of time between start and end date (using censured end date which is: The end date of the child's legal status and, if none, the end of the period under study.)
### code legal_status into three groups: dual ward, state ward, and county ward (no county wards present)
legal_details <- new_legal_details %>%
  distinct(.,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% ### file already unique; no pure duplicates and no records dropped
  mutate(LEGAL_STATUS_BEGIN = ymd(LEGAL_STATUS_BEGIN),
         CENSURED_STATUS_END = ymd(CENSURED_STATUS_END),
         legal_status_begin_end_diff_days = time_length(difftime(CENSURED_STATUS_END, LEGAL_STATUS_BEGIN), unit = 'days')) %>% 
  arrange(PERSON_ID,LEGAL_STATUS_BEGIN,desc(legal_status_begin_end_diff_days)) %>% 
  distinct(PERSON_ID,LEGAL_STATUS_BEGIN, .keep_all=TRUE) %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  mutate(legal_status_unique_id = paste0(person_id,legal_status_begin,legal_status)) %>% 
  mutate(legal_status_ward_flag = case_when(
    legal_status %in% state_ward_status_list ~ 1,
    legal_status %in% dual_ward_status_list ~ 2,
    legal_status %in% county_ward_status_list ~ 3,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    legal_status_ward_flag = factor(legal_status_ward_flag,
         levels = c(1,2,3),
         labels = c("State Ward","Dual Ward", "County Ward"))) ### use factor function to assign labels to values

###### de-dup jj_assessments using all columns
jj_assessments <- new_assessments %<>%
  distinct(.,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(ASSESSMENT_DATE = as.Date(as.numeric(ASSESSMENT_DATE), "1899-12-30"),
         ASSESSMENT_DATE = ymd(ASSESSMENT_DATE)) ### file already unique; no pure duplicates and no records dropped 

### create assessments file with only dispositional assessment data -- we'll just focus on these data in analysis
jj_assessments_disposition <- jj_assessments %>% 
  filter(ASSESSMENT_TYPE=="DISPOSITIONAL ASSESSMENT")

###### fuzzy join of child_details_placements and jj_assessments -- using match_fun to specify that the assessment date must be less than or equal to the placement date -- if this doesn't work, just match on dispositional assessments, keep <= placement date, calculate days to placement, and only keep smallest one
jj_assessments_placement <- 
  fuzzy_left_join(child_details_placements,jj_assessments_disposition,
                  by = c("PERSON_ID" = "PERSON_ID",
                         "PLACEMENT_BEGIN_DATE" = "ASSESSMENT_DATE"),
                  match_fun = list(`==`, `>=`)) %>% 
  mutate(assessment_placement_diff = time_length(difftime(PLACEMENT_BEGIN_DATE, ASSESSMENT_DATE), unit = 'days'),
         assessment_placement_diff_less_548 = ifelse(assessment_placement_diff<=548,1,0)) %>% ### calculate time between assessment and placement; using 548 as a year a half delineator -- in part b/c some youth are given risk assessment in the middle of a longer placement (at least as it appears in the data) and this would allow the risk data to more consistently be linked to the following placement
   mutate_at(vars(ASSESSMENT_TYPE:assessment_placement_diff_less_548),
       funs(replace(., assessment_placement_diff_less_548 == 0, NA))) %>%   ### recode all assessment data with assessment data/placement date differences larger than 548 days to NA
  dplyr::rename(PERSON_ID = PERSON_ID.x) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-PERSON_ID.y) %>% ### keep person_id from child_details_placements
  arrange(PERSON_ID,PROVIDER_ID,PLACEMENT_BEGIN_DATE,PLACE_NO,assessment_placement_diff) %>% ### when there are duplicates, we are keeping the record with the smallest `assessment_placement_diff` value (the assessment closest to the placement date)
  distinct(PERSON_ID,PROVIDER_ID,PLACEMENT_BEGIN_DATE,PLACE_NO, .keep_all=TRUE) ### de-dup by unique placement; record count should now match original record count in placement data file

### until we receive and validate 'placement episode ID' from MDHHS, i am creating my own placement episode rank variable to associate placements that occur continuously from those separated by more than 15 days; the current MDHHS data ranks all placements in youth's file -- making it difficult to separately group, for example, two continuous placements in a youth's early childhood from three continuous placements in that youth's teens
### they are working to provide us with a 'placement episode ID' which should theoretically fix this issue, btw it's TBD
### placement_episode_segment ranks the placement episodes for a given kid (three separate periods of continuous placements would be 1,2,3 respectively for each unique placement within the episode)
### placement_episode_no ranks the unique placements within each placement episode
### create place_no_of_earliest_disposition_assess to note the earliest placement within an episode for which there is an assessment
### create disposition_risk_level_earliest to note the risk level associated with the earliest assessment within an episode
jj_assessments_placement_ordered <- jj_assessments_placement %>% 
  group_by(PERSON_ID) %>%
  # arrange(PERSON_ID,PLACEMENT_BEGIN_DATE) %>%
  mutate(next_placement_begin_date = PLACEMENT_BEGIN_DATE[PLACE_NO = PLACE_NO + 1],
         next_placement_begin_date_diff = time_length(difftime(next_placement_begin_date,PLACEMENT_END_DATE), unit = 'days'),
         next_placement_begin_date_diff_more_than_15 = ifelse((next_placement_begin_date_diff>15 | is.na(next_placement_begin_date)==TRUE),PLACE_NO,0),
         start_new_placement_episode_flag = ifelse(lag(next_placement_begin_date_diff_more_than_15) > 0, 1, 0),
         start_new_placement_episode_flag = ifelse(is.na(start_new_placement_episode_flag)==TRUE, 0, start_new_placement_episode_flag),
         placement_episode_segment_manual_count = cumsum(c(TRUE,diff(start_new_placement_episode_flag)==1))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(PERSON_ID,placement_episode_segment_manual_count) %>%
  arrange(PERSON_ID,placement_episode_segment_manual_count,PLACEMENT_BEGIN_DATE) %>%
  mutate(placement_episode_no_manual_count = order(PLACEMENT_BEGIN_DATE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(PERSON_ID,PLCMNT_EPISODE_ID) %>%
  arrange(PERSON_ID,PLCMNT_EPISODE_ID,PLACEMENT_BEGIN_DATE) %>%
  mutate(placement_episode_no = order(PLACEMENT_BEGIN_DATE),
         placement_episode_final_end_date = PLACEMENT_END_DATE[placement_episode_no == max(placement_episode_no)],
         placement_episode_first_start_date = PLACEMENT_BEGIN_DATE[placement_episode_no == min(placement_episode_no)]) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  group_by(PERSON_ID) %>%
  arrange(PERSON_ID,PLCMNT_EPISODE_ID,placement_episode_first_start_date) %>% 
  mutate(placement_episode_segment = dense_rank(placement_episode_first_start_date)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  group_by(PERSON_ID,PLCMNT_EPISODE_ID) %>%
  mutate(place_no_of_earliest_disposition_assess = ifelse(!is.na(DISP_FINAL_RISK_LEVEL)==TRUE, min(placement_episode_no[!is.na(DISP_FINAL_RISK_LEVEL)==TRUE]),NA),
         place_no_of_earliest_disposition_assess = min(place_no_of_earliest_disposition_assess[!is.na(place_no_of_earliest_disposition_assess)==TRUE]),
         disposition_risk_level_earliest = DISP_FINAL_RISK_LEVEL[min(place_no_of_earliest_disposition_assess)]) %>% 
  ungroup()

```{r include=FALSE}
### clean dates, create race/ethnicity var with both four and six values, and create sex flag
jj_assessments_placement_legal_status_clean <- jj_assessments_placement_legal_status %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  mutate(birth_dt = ymd(birth_dt),
         assessment_date = ymd(assessment_date),
         removal_date = ymd(removal_date),
         discharge_date = ymd(discharge_date),
         placement_begin_date = ymd(placement_begin_date),
         placement_end_date = ymd(placement_end_date),
         placement_begin_date_year = year(placement_begin_date),
         placement_end_date_year = year(placement_end_date),
         age_placement_start = time_length(difftime(placement_begin_date, birth_dt), "years")) %>% 
  group_by(person_id,placement_episode_segment) %>% 
  mutate(placement_episode_begin_date = placement_begin_date[min(placement_episode_no)],
         placement_episode_end_date = placement_end_date[max(placement_episode_no)],
         placement_episode_start_year = placement_begin_date_year[min(placement_episode_no)],
         placement_episode_end_year = placement_end_date_year[max(placement_episode_no)]) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(age_placement_start<21) %>% ### using this as additional data check -- got number from soleil -- confirm
  mutate(race_csg_4 = case_when(
    multi_race=="Black/African American" & hispanic_latino_ind!="YES" ~ 1,
    hispanic_latino_ind=="YES" ~ 2,
    multi_race=="White" & hispanic_latino_ind!="YES" ~ 3,
    multi_race %in% c("American Indian/Alaskan Native","White, American Indian/Alaskan Native","American Indian/Alaskan Native, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander") ~ 4,
    multi_race %in% c("Asian","Black/African American, American Indian/Alaskan Native","Black/African American, Asian","Black/African American, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","Unable to Determine","Unknown","White, Asian","White, Black/African American","White, Black/African American, American Indian/Alaskan Native","White, Black/African American, Asian","White, Black/African American, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","White, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander") & hispanic_latino_ind!="YES" ~ 5,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    race_csg_4 = factor(race_csg_4,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5),
         labels = c("Black", "Hispanic", "White","American Indian/Alaskan Native", "Other"))) %>%  ### use factor function to assign labels to values
  mutate(gender_clean = case_when(
    gender_txt=="Female" ~ 1,
    gender_txt=="Male" ~ 2,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    gender_clean = factor(gender_clean,
         levels = c(1,2),
         labels = c("Female", "Male"))) ### use factor function to assign labels to values

### clean dates, create race/ethnicity var with both four and six values, and create sex flag for child_details_incidents file
child_details_incidents_clean <- child_details_incidents %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  mutate(birth_dt = ymd(birth_dt),
         incident_date = ymd(incident_date),

    multi_race %in% c("Asian","Black/African American, American Indian/Alaskan Native","Black/African American, Asian","Black/African American, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","Unable to Determine","Unknown","White, Asian","White, Black/African American","White, Black/African American, American Indian/Alaskan Native","White, Black/African American, Asian","White, Black/African American, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","White, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander") & hispanic_latino_ind!="YES" ~ 5,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    race_csg_4 = factor(race_csg_4,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5),
         labels = c("Black", "Hispanic", "White","American Indian/Alaskan Native", "Other"))) %>%  ### use factor function to assign labels to values
  mutate(gender_clean = case_when(
    gender_txt=="Female" ~ 1,
    gender_txt=="Male" ~ 2,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    gender_clean = factor(gender_clean,
         levels = c(1,2),

```{r include=FALSE}
### apply additional business rules from josh and soleil:

#1.
#	Remove detention/jail from as well as the following in-home placements unique placement pool and placement episode: "Detention", "Jail", "Adoptive Home", "Parental Home", "Friend/Partner Home", "Licensed/Unlicensed Relative Home", "Unrelated Caregiver", "College Dormitory", "Boarding School, etc. (other)", "Terminated parental home", "Out of State Parental Home", "Out of State Licensed Relative", "Out of State Unlicensed Relative", "AWOL", "Escape", "Independent Living", "Rental Home/Apartment", "Pre-Adoptive Home", "NO MATCH FOUND"

jj_assessments_placement_legal_status_clean %<>%
  mutate(placement_does_not_count_overall = ifelse(living_arrangement %in% c("Detention", "Jail", "Adoptive Home", "Parental Home", "Friend/Partner Home", "Licensed/Unlicensed Relative Home", "Unrelated Caregiver", "College Dormitory", "Boarding School, etc. (other)", "Terminated parental home", "Out of State Parental Home", "Out of State Licensed Relative", "Out of State Unlicensed Relative", "AWOL", "Escape", "Independent Living", "Rental Home/Apartment", "Pre-Adoptive Home", "NO MATCH FOUND"),1,0),
         placement_does_not_count_in_home_only = ifelse(living_arrangement %in% c("Adoptive Home", "Parental Home", "Friend/Partner Home", "Licensed/Unlicensed Relative Home", "Unrelated Caregiver", "College Dormitory", "Boarding School, etc. (other)", "Terminated parental home", "Out of State Parental Home", "Out of State Licensed Relative", "Out of State Unlicensed Relative", "Independent Living", "Rental Home/Apartment", "Pre-Adoptive Home", "NO MATCH FOUND"),1,0))


# This leaves the following living arrangements as placements which can constitute a placement episode, count as unique individual placements, count towards placements per episode, and count towards length of stay: "Adult Foster Home", "Agency" (indicates "a youth is in an office overnight (at midnight)"), "Child Caring Institution", "Court Treatment Facility", "Emergency Residential Shelter", "Emergency Shelter Home", "EPIC Guardianship Home", "Hospital", "Mental Health Facility", "Juvenile Guardianship Home", "Licensed Unrelated Foster Home", "Out of State Child Caring Institution", "Out of State Foster Home", "Private Agency Foster Care", "Runaway Service Facility", "MDHHS Training School","Community Justice Center" (closed prior to study window)

jj_assessments_placement_legal_status_clean %<>%
  mutate(placement_does_count = ifelse(living_arrangement %in% c("Adult Foster Home", "Agency", "Child Caring Institution", "Court Treatment Facility", "Emergency Residential Shelter", "Emergency Shelter Home", "EPIC Guardianship Home", "Hospital", "Mental Health Facility", "Juvenile Guardianship Home", "Licensed Unrelated Foster Home", "Out of State Child Caring Institution", "Out of State Foster Home", "Private Agency Foster Care", "Runaway Service Facility", "MDHHS Training School","Community Justice Center"),1,0),
         placement_does_count_plus_det_jail = ifelse(living_arrangement %in% c("Detention","Jail","Adult Foster Home", "Agency", "Child Caring Institution", "Court Treatment Facility", "Emergency Residential Shelter", "Emergency Shelter Home", "EPIC Guardianship Home", "Hospital", "Mental Health Facility", "Juvenile Guardianship Home", "Licensed Unrelated Foster Home", "Out of State Child Caring Institution", "Out of State Foster Home", "Private Agency Foster Care", "Runaway Service Facility", "MDHHS Training School","Community Justice Center"),1,0))

#2. Separate out placement episodes that only include in-home supervision for secure/non-secure facility analysis 
jj_assessments_placement_legal_status_clean %<>%
  group_by(person_id,placement_episode_segment) %>% 
  mutate(placement_episode_placement_does_count_total = sum(placement_does_count),
         placement_episode_placement_does_count_with_det_jail_total = sum(placement_does_count_plus_det_jail),
         placement_episode_placement_does_count_total_none = ifelse(placement_episode_placement_does_count_total==0,1,0),
         placement_episode_placement_does_count_with_det_jail_total_none = ifelse(placement_episode_placement_does_count_with_det_jail_total==0,1,0),
         placement_episode_filter_out = ifelse(placement_episode_placement_does_count_total_none==0,1,0)) %>% 
  ungroup()

### 642/9,765 observations (post dropping record with no legal status) have no out of home placement -- including either detention or jail

### 2,249/9,765 observations (post dropping record with no legal status) have no out of home placement -- not counting either detention or jail

Drop placement episodes with no legal status in legal_details table -- indicates that actual associated legal status not JJ or dual ward (records were pulled because a JJ case wasn't closed or because it is simply an A/N placement episode that occurred before a dual ward/JJ placement episode in our study window -- and also happens to be in our study window; i.e. a kid has an A/N placement episode from 2015-2016, in the study window, and then a dual ward placement episode from 2017-2018 -- we would have both episodes but only the legal status associated with the second episode b/c it is JJ-involved)

#### Legal Status: Dual, State, and County Wards in Data

NOTE/QUESTION: Need to confirm two things about legal status; 1 -- that coding of dual ward, state ward, county ward is correct and buckets make sense (not sure if there's a way to distinguish county wards placed in state facilities versus county wards whose caseworkers simply entered their data into MiSACWIS, though?) and 2 -- the best way to link legal status to placement data with only person_id and dates? 

No missing data -- each youth has at least one corresponding legal_status record. 

For now, I've coded the following legal statuses as dual ward, based on Mike's feedback: 
52 - MCI Ward/44 and Act 150/46 -- mdhhs (abuse/neglect whose rights have been terminated and delinquent public ward under act 150 w/ mdhhs)
90 - Temp Court Ward 42 and Delinquent Court Ward 40 -- uncertain (a/n temp court and delinquent court ward; use other field for court, mdhhs, can change over time)
91 -  Perm Court Ward 41 and Delinquent Court Ward 40 -- uncertain ()
92 - Temp Court Ward 42 and Act 150/46 -- mdhhs
93 - Perm Court Ward 41 and Act 150/46 -- mdhhs
94 - MCI Ward/44 and Delinquent Court Ward/40 -- uncertain
80 - In Home 42 and Delinquent Court Ward 40 -- uncertain
82 - In Home 42 and Act 150/46 -- mdhhs

And the following as state wards based on Soleil's feedback (according to Soleil, "Both the 40 and the 50 are MDHHS supervised youth, not county court supervised. The 50 is the legal status fort given when an intake is done in MiSACWIS until another status is added based on a court order or the youth may be a pre sentence investigation"):
40 - Court Ward Delinquent -- mdhhs
44 - State Ward ' MCI - Act 220/296
46 - State Ward - Delinquent - Act 150 -- mdhhs
50 - Non-Ward With a Delinquent Petition Filed -- either intake, juvenile competency, or pretrial investigations AND likely mdhhs supervised

<br>

```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### create three lists for dual, state, and county wards with the corresponding legal_status codes 
dual_ward_status_list <- c("52 - MCI Ward/44 and Act 150/46","90 - Temp Court Ward 42 and Delinquent Court Ward 40","91 -  Perm Court Ward 41 and Delinquent Court Ward 40","92 - Temp Court Ward 42 and Act 150/46","93 - Perm Court Ward 41 and Act 150/46","94 - MCI Ward/44 and Delinquent Court Ward/40","80 - In Home 42 and Delinquent Court Ward 40","82 - In Home 42 and Act 150/46")

state_ward_status_list <- c("40 - Court Ward Delinquent","46 - State Ward - Delinquent - Act 150","50 - Non-Ward With a Delinquent Petition Filed")

county_ward_status_list <- c()

### code legal_status into three groups: dual ward, state ward, and county ward
legal_status %<>%
  clean_names() %>% 
  mutate(legal_status_unique_id = paste0(person_id,legal_status_begin,legal_status)) %>% 
  mutate(legal_status_ward_flag = case_when(
    legal_status %in% state_ward_status_list ~ 1,
    legal_status %in% dual_ward_status_list ~ 2,
    legal_status %in% county_ward_status_list ~ 3,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    legal_status_ward_flag = factor(legal_status_ward_flag,
         levels = c(1,2,3),
         labels = c("State Ward","Dual Ward", "County Ward"))) ### use factor function to assign labels to values

### all -- grouped by year
legal_status_grouped <- legal_status %>% 
  distinct(legal_status_unique_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(legal_status)==TRUE) %>% 
  group_by(legal_status_ward_flag) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(legal_status_unique_id),
            `Percent of Total Legal Status File Sample (%)` = round(n_distinct(legal_status_unique_id)/14721*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(`Legal Status` = legal_status_ward_flag) 

### all -- overall
legal_status_overall <- legal_status %>% 
  distinct(legal_status_unique_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(legal_status)==TRUE) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(legal_status_unique_id),
            `Percent of Total Legal Status File Sample (%)` = round(n_distinct(legal_status_unique_id)/`Unique Count (N)`*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(`Legal Status` = "Overall") 

### combine tables for kable
legal_status_table <- rbind(legal_status_grouped,legal_status_overall)

### print table via kableextra
kable(legal_status_table, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), align=rep('c')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"), row_label_position = "l") %>% 
  row_spec(3, bold = TRUE)
```

#### Age at Beginning of Placement (unique by individual and year of placement)
NOTE: Excluding all ages below 7 and above 19.5 as these seem most likely to be data entry errors (either with placement date or date of birth) -- does this make sense? Using this rule, we lose about 2,000 records (unique individuals by year)
```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### create age bins
child_details_placements_offense_assess_clean %<>%
  mutate(age_placement_start = time_length(difftime(placement_begin_date, birth_dt), "years")) %>% 
  group_by(person_id,placement_begin_date_year) %>% 
  mutate(age_placement_start_min = min(age_placement_start)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(age_placement_start_min_bin = case_when(
    age_placement_start_min>=7 & age_placement_start_min<10 ~ 1,
    age_placement_start_min>=10 & age_placement_start_min<13 ~ 2,
    age_placement_start_min>=13 & age_placement_start_min<16 ~ 3,
    age_placement_start_min>=16 & age_placement_start_min<18 ~ 4,
    age_placement_start_min>=18 & age_placement_start_min<=19.5 ~ 5, ### using 19.5 for now; i figure this indicates that the youth's offense was committed prior to 18th birthday but timing of detention was after 18th birthday? double check with emily
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    age_placement_start_min_bin = factor(age_placement_start_min_bin,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5),
         labels = c("Less than 10", "10 to 13", "13 to 16","16 to 18","18+"))) ### use factor function to assign labels to values

### create detention table by race/ethnicity -- removing 'unknown' for both tables

  dplyr::group_by(age_placement_start_min_bin) %>% 
 summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(person_id,placement_begin_date_year),
           `Percent of Total Sample (%)` = round(n_distinct(person_id,placement_begin_date_year)/13695*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>%

### create overall detention table 
placement_overall_age_table <- child_details_placements_offense_assess_clean %>%

#### Academic Data -- not comprehensive of all youth (only 2443 of 5695 youth have data in academic_evaluations data file -- 57%) and can only potentially link to placement data via dates (as we only have person_id otherwise)
```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### inner join academic_evaluations to child_details -- dropping records from child_details with no matching placement data
child_details_academic <- inner_join(child_details, academic_evaluations, by = "PERSON_ID") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  mutate(disability_504_flag = ifelse(!is.na(disability_504_begin_dt)==TRUE,1,0),
         grade_lvl = ifelse(grade_lvl %in% c("GED","GED Complete","Post Secondary","Diploma Complete","12+"),13,grade_lvl)) %>% 
  group_by(person_id) %>% 
  mutate(disability_504_flag = ifelse(sum(disability_504_flag, na.rm = TRUE)>0,1,0),
         academic_delay_poor_attendance_flag = ifelse(sum(academic_delay_poor_attendance, na.rm = TRUE)>0,1,0),
         min_grade_lvl = min(as.numeric(grade_lvl)),
         max_grade_lvl = max(as.numeric(grade_lvl)),
         min_eval_date = min(ymd(evaluation_date)),
         max_eval_date = max(ymd(evaluation_date))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  distinct(person_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(eval_time_span_first_last = time_length(difftime(max_eval_date, min_eval_date), "years"),
         grade_lvl_difference = max_grade_lvl - min_grade_lvl,
         grade_per_year = round(grade_lvl_difference/eval_time_span_first_last, digits = 1)) 

### create detention table by grade level
placement_acad_grade_level_table <- child_details_academic %>% 
  filter(!is.na(min_grade_lvl)==TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(min_grade_lvl) %>% 
 summarise(`% Disability 504` = round(n_distinct(person_id[disability_504_flag==1])/n_distinct(person_id)*100, digits = 2),
           `% Academic Delay due to Poor Attendance` = round(n_distinct(person_id[academic_delay_poor_attendance_flag==1])/n_distinct(person_id)*100, digits = 2),
           `Grades Advanced per Year, Median ('1.0' is 1 grade advanced per year)` = median(grade_per_year, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::rename(`Grade of First Evaluation` = min_grade_lvl)

### create overall grade level table 
placement_acad_overall_table <- child_details_academic %>% 
  filter(!is.na(min_grade_lvl)==TRUE) %>%
  summarise(`% Disability 504` = round(n_distinct(person_id[disability_504_flag==1])/n_distinct(person_id)*100, digits = 2),
           `% Academic Delay due to Poor Attendance` = round(n_distinct(person_id[academic_delay_poor_attendance_flag==1])/n_distinct(person_id)*100, digits = 2),
           `Grades Advanced per Year, Median ('1.0' is 1 grade advanced per year)` = median(grade_per_year,na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(`Grade of First Evaluation` = "Overall")

### merge grade level and overall tables via rbind
placement_acad_grade_level_table_final <- rbind(placement_acad_grade_level_table,placement_acad_overall_table)

### print table via kableextra
kable(placement_acad_grade_level_table_final, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), align=rep('c')) %>%
   kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"), row_label_position = "l") %>% 
  row_spec(14, bold = TRUE)
```

#### Placements Over Time

NOTE/QUESTION: Defining unique placement -- one individual can have multiple cases which may include multiple placements. At what level should be group placements? For now, I'll group in two ways -- both overall placement counts AND individuals placed. 'place_no' in the placements file appears to number a youth's placement for the entirety of their involvement with DHHS (so for someone with three placements, each placement is labelled as either 1, 2, or 3). We could use this to group all placements by youth, if need be.

Other outstanding questions: Treatment of multiple placements for one case/referral (leave as separate placements or group together)? Interpretation and coding of AWOL status?

            `Low (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_assessment_id[risk_level=="Low"])/`Total (N)`*100, digits = 2),
            `Moderate (N)` = n_distinct(unique_assessment_id[risk_level=="Moderate"]),
            `Moderate (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_assessment_id[risk_level=="Moderate"])/`Total (N)`*100, digits = 2),
            `High (N)` = n_distinct(unique_assessment_id[risk_level=="High"]),
            `High (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_assessment_id[risk_level=="High"])/`Total (N)`*100, digits = 2)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(`Assessment Type` = assessment_type)

### print table via kableextra
kable(case_plans_jj_assessment_grouped, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), align=rep('c')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"), row_label_position = "l") 
```

## Incidents

- Incidents over time (not standardized with placements, yet, however)
- Incident type (may need some clarification of meaning of certain incident groupings -- like seclusion)
- Incident count by placement/provider type 
- Youth restraint flag by placement/provider type

<br>

#### Incidents over time (not standardized with placements, yet, however)
```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
incidents %<>%
  clean_names() %>% 
  distinct(person_id,incident_id,incident_type, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% ### de-dup by incident (only three duplicates)
  mutate(incident_date = ymd(incident_date),
         incident_year = year(incident_date),
         incident_unique_id = paste0(person_id,incident_id,incident_type))

### all -- grouped by year
incidents_overall_count_year <- incidents %>% 
  distinct(incident_unique_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(incident_year)==TRUE) %>% 
  group_by(incident_year) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(incident_unique_id),
            `Percent of Total Sample (%)` = round(n_distinct(incident_unique_id)/53384*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(`Year of Incident` = incident_year) %>% 
  mutate(`Year of Incident` = as.character(`Year of Incident`))

### all -- overall
incidents_overall_count_total <- incidents %>% 
  distinct(incident_unique_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(incident_year)==TRUE) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(incident_unique_id),
            `Percent of Total Sample (%)` = round(n_distinct(incident_unique_id)/53384*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(`Year of Incident` = "Overall") 

### combine tables for kable
incidents_overall_count_year_table <- rbind(incidents_overall_count_year,incidents_overall_count_total)

### print table via kableextra
kable(incidents_overall_count_year_table, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), align=rep('c')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"), row_label_position = "l") %>% 
  row_spec(9, bold = TRUE)
```
